lessons.name: var / let / const
lessons.desc: Three ways to declare variables — differ in scope, hoisting, and mutability.
lessons.q: Explain the difference between var, let, and const. When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: Tricky follow-up: What happens when you try to re-declare a const object's property?
terms: Wo ilaaka jahan variable dikhta hai.
Ussi naam se dobara variable banana.
lessons.what:
Teen tarike hain variable banane ke, aur teen cheezon mein farak hai: scope, hoisting, aur badal sakte ho ya nahi.

var purana hai — poore function mein dikhta hai. let aur const naye hain — sirf apne { } block mein dikhte hain.
lessons.why: var ki do bimariyan thin: wo if/for ke block se bahar leak ho jaata tha, aur usko dobara declare karna chal jaata tha (jisse galti se purani value mit jaati thi). let/const ne dono band kiye.

pros: const se pata chal jaata hai ki value badlegi nahi.
Block scope se variable leak nahi hota.
Re-declare band — galti se purani value mitegi nahi.
cons: const object ko immutable nahi banata — sabse badi galatfehmi.
TDZ ki wajah se declare se pehle use karne par error (par ye achha hai).
Purane browsers mein let/const ke liye transpile chahiye.
gotchas: const arr = [] ke baad arr.push(1) chalta hai. const sirf re-assign rokta hai.
var ki value hoisting mein undefined milti hai, let mein error.
Global scope mein var x window.x ban jaata hai, let x nahi.

lessons.name: Primitive vs Reference Types
lessons.desc: Primitives are copied by value; objects/arrays are copied by reference.
lessons.q: What is the difference between primitive and reference types in JavaScript?
lessons.qsub: What does shallow copy vs deep copy mean? When does it matter?
terms: Simple value — number, string, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint.
Object, array, function — inka pata (address) variable mein rehta hai, khud value nahi.
lessons.what:
Primitive variable mein value khud rehti hai. Copy karoge to nayi alag value banti hai.

Reference variable mein sirf pata rehta hai — asli object kahin aur (heap mein) hota hai. Copy karoge to pata copy hota hai, object nahi. Do naam, ek hi ghar.
lessons.analogy:
Primitive = kisi ko photo ki copy dena. Wo apni copy phaad de to aapki safe hai.
Reference = ghar ka pata dena. Wo jaakar deewar rang de to aapke ghar mein hi rang lagega.
lessons.why: Ye JavaScript ke sabse zyada bug isi se aate hain — "maine to copy banayi thi, original kaise badal gaya?" Aur === objects par kyu false deta hai, uska jawab bhi yahi hai: wo pate compare karta hai, andar ka saaman nahi.

where: "Maine copy banayi thi, original kaise badla?" — 90% cases mein yahi wajah.
State immutably update karna padta hai — warna React ko pata hi nahi chalta ki kuch badla.

pros: Reference se bade objects pass karna sasta hai — poora data copy nahi hota.
Ek jagah badlo, sab jagah dikhta hai (jab yahi chahiye ho).
Primitives hamesha safe hain — unhe copy karne mein koi khatra nahi.
cons: Anjaane mein original badal jaata hai — sabse aam JS bug.
=== objects par kaam nahi karta.
Shallow vs deep copy ka farak yaad rakhna padta hai.
gotchas: [...arr] aur {...obj} shallow hain — sirf ek level copy karte hain.

typeof null "object" deta hai — ye JS ka purana bug hai jo kabhi theek nahi hua.

lessons.name: null vs undefined vs NaN
lessons.desc: Three "empty" values with different semantics: intentional absence, uninitialized, and failed numeric op.
lessons.q: What is the difference between null, undefined, and NaN? How do you reliably check for each?
lessons.qsub: Why is typeof null === "object" a bug, and how do you work around it?
terms: Value di hi nahi gayi — JS ne khud lagayi.
Value jaan-boojh kar khaali rakhi gayi — aapne lagayi.
Not a Number — number wala kaam fail ho gaya.
lessons.what:
Teeno "kuch nahi" jaise lagte hain, par unka matlab alag hai:

undefined = "kisi ne value di hi nahi". null = "maine jaan-boojh kar khaali rakha". NaN = "number banane ki koshish ki, ban nahi paya".
lessons.analogy: Form ka ek field. undefined = field abhi tak dikha hi nahi. null = field dikha, user ne "N/A" likha. NaN = user ne umar mein "abc" likh diya.
lessons.why: Farak isliye maayne rakhta hai kyunki undefined aksar bug hota hai ("value aayi hi nahi") aur null aksar valid hota hai ("khaali hai, aur ye theek hai"). API design mein bhi: null lautana matlab "dhoondha, mila nahi"; undefined matlab "shayad maine dekha hi nahi".
lessons.code:
let a;                    // undefined — JS ne lagaya
let b = null;             // null — maine lagaya

typeof undefined          // "undefined"
typeof null               // "object"   ← purana JS bug
Number.isNaN(0/0)         // true

// ?? sirf null/undefined par default deta hai:
0 || "default"            // "default"   ✗ 0 valid tha!
0 ?? "default"            // 0           ✓

// ?. — bina crash ke andar jhaanko:
user?.address?.city       // undefined agar kuch bhi missing ho
where: ?? use karo, || nahi — warna 0 aur "" bhi replace ho jaate hain.
Field ka null hona matlab "khaali hai"; undefined matlab "aaya hi nahi".
obj?.a?.b se crash bache bina lambi if chain ke.
pros: ?? aur ?. ne is poore area ko aasan bana diya.
Do alag matlab hone se code ka iraada saaf dikhta hai.
x == null se dono ek saath check ho jaate hain.
cons: typeof null ka "object" dena aaj bhi confuse karta hai.
Do "khaali" values hona apne aap mein ek design galti maani jaati hai.
NaN khud ke barabar nahi hota.
gotchas: || aur ?? mein farak: || har falsy par default deta hai, ?? sirf null/undefined par.
typeof null === "object" — pehchanne ke liye x === null likho.
Function ka koi return na ho to wo undefined lautata hai, null nahi.

lessons.name: Type Coercion
lessons.desc: JS automatically converts types when mixing incompatible values in operations.
lessons.q: Explain implicit vs explicit type coercion. Why is 0 == false true but 0 === false false?
lessons.qsub: What does [] + {} produce and why?
terms: JS ka khud-ba-khud type badal dena.
Aapne nahi bola, JS ne khud kiya — "5" * 2.
lessons.what:
Jab do alag types ko mila do, JS unhe ek jaisa banane ki koshish karta hai — chahe uska matlab bane ya na bane.

Do niyam yaad rakho: + string ki taraf jhukta hai (agar ek bhi string ho to jodna nahi, chipkana hota hai). Baaki saare operators number ki taraf jhukte hain.
lessons.why: JS shuru mein aisi language banai gayi thi jo "kabhi crash na kare" — isliye wo galat cheezon ko bhi chala deta hai. Faayda ye ki quick script likhna aasan, nuksaan ye ki bug crash nahi karta, chup-chaap galat jawab deta hai.
lessons.code:
"5" + 2      // "52"    <- + string ki taraf jhuka
"5" - 2      // 3       <- - number ki taraf
"5" * "2"    // 10

1 + true     // 2       <- true → 1
1 + null     // 1       <- null → 0
1 + undefined// NaN     <- undefined → NaN

[] + {}      // "[object Object]"
[] + []      // ""

// SAHI TARIKA — khud badlo:
Number("5")     // 5
String(5)       // "5"
Boolean("")     // false
parseInt("5px") // 5      <- Number("5px") NaN deta
where: Input hamesha string deta hai — Number() lagana zaroori hai, warna "5" + 1 = "51".
if (value) mein value boolean banti hai — falsy list yaad honi chahiye.
"Ye kya print karega" wale trick sawaal isi se aate hain.
pros: Quick scripts likhna aasan — types ka jhanjhat nahi.
if (arr.length) jaisa chhota code likh sakte ho.
Template literal mein sab kuch apne aap string ban jaata hai.
cons: Bug crash nahi karta — chup-chaap galat jawab deta hai.
Niyam yaad rakhne padte hain, guess kaam nahi aata.
TypeScript ke bina inme se bahut galtiyan pakdi hi nahi jaatin.
gotchas: Falsy list yaad karo: false, 0, -0, "", null, undefined, NaN. Baaki sab truthy — [] aur {} bhi.
NaN === NaN false hai. Check karne ke liye Number.isNaN() use karo.
parseInt("08") aaj theek hai par hamesha radix do: parseInt("08", 10).

lessons.name: == vs === (Abstract vs Strict Equality)
lessons.desc: == allows type coercion; === checks value AND type without conversion.
lessons.q: When would you ever want to use == over ===? Give a real use case.
lessons.qsub: What does Object.is() add over ===?
terms: Type badal kar compare karta hai.
Type bhi same hona chahiye, tabhi true.
=== jaisa, par NaN aur -0 ko theek se handle karta hai.
lessons.what:
=== seedha hai: type same + value same, tabhi true.

== pehle types ko ek jaisa banata hai, phir compare karta hai. Isi "pehle badalna" mein sab gadbad hoti hai.
lessons.why: Ek hi asli jagah hai jahan == kaam ka hai: x == null — ye null aur undefined dono ek saath pakad leta hai. Baaki har jagah === use karo.

lessons.code:
0 == false        // true    ✗ confusing
0 === false       // false   ✓ saaf

null == undefined  // true   <- yahi ek kaam ka case
null === undefined // false

NaN === NaN            // false  !
Object.is(NaN, NaN)    // true   ✓

// Objects hamesha pata compare karte hain:
{a:1} === {a:1}   // false

// PRACTICAL:
if (x == null) { }        // ✓ null YA undefined
if (x === null) { }       // sirf null
where: Default hamesha ===. Linter mein eqeqeq rule on rakho.
if (x == null) — do check ek line mein.
pros: === ka behaviour hamesha predictable hai.
x == null ek chhota kaam ka shortcut hai.
Object.is NaN aur -0 ke edge cases theek karta hai.
cons: == ke niyam yaad karne layak nahi hain — sirf table hai.
=== bhi objects par pata compare karta hai, content nahi.
NaN ka behaviour ajeeb hai aur bhoolna aasan.
gotchas: NaN === NaN false hai — duniya ki ek hi value jo apne barabar nahi.
[] == false true hai par if ([]) chalta hai — dono niyam alag hain.
Interview mein "== kabhi use karte ho?" ka jawab: "sirf x == null ke liye."

lessons.name: Destructuring & Spread/Rest
lessons.desc: Syntactic patterns to unpack values from arrays/objects and gather/spread elements.
lessons.q: Explain destructuring with default values, renaming, and nested patterns. What about rest/spread?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between rest parameters and the arguments object?
terms: Object/array se values seedha variables mein nikalna.
Bache hue elements ek jagah jama karna.
Ek cheez ko khol kar phailana.
lessons.what:
Destructuring se object/array ke andar se values seedha nikal sakte ho — bina obj.a, obj.b likhe.

... do kaam karta hai: rest (bache hue jama karo) aur spread (khol kar phailao). Jagah se pata chalta hai kaunsa hai.
lessons.why: Iske bina function ke arguments ka order yaad rakhna padta tha (draw(10, 0, "red") — kaunsa kya?). Destructuring se arguments ko naam mil jaate hain, defaults ek jagah aa jaate hain, aur immutable update ({ ...state, x: 1 }) ek line ka kaam ban jaata hai.
where: Named arguments jaisa — order yaad nahi rakhna padta.
pros: Code chhota aur padhne mein saaf.
Default values ek hi jagah.
Immutable updates bahut aasan.
cons: Deep nesting padhne mein bhaari ho jaati hai.
Spread shallow hai — nested objects share hote hain.
Har spread naya object banata hai — hot loop mein cost.
gotchas: undefined par default lagta hai, null par nahi. { a = 1 } se null hi milega.
Function param ko = {} default do, warna bina argument bulane par crash.
Spread shallow hai — nested object dono jagah share hoga.

lessons.name: Map & Set — when to use over objects, iteration, performance
lessons.desc: Map preserves insertion order, accepts any key type, has size property. Set stores unique values. Both have O(1) lookup like objects but better for non-string keys. WeakMap/WeakSet allow garbage collection of keys.
lessons.q: What is the difference between Map and plain objects? When would you use Set over an array?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between WeakMap and Map? Why are WeakMap keys not enumerable?
terms: Key-value store jahan key kuch bhi ho sakti hai, aur order yaad rehta hai.
lessons.what:
Object bhi key-value rakhta hai — phir Map kyu?

Teen wajah: Map ki key kuch bhi ho sakti hai (object, function), usme insertion order pakka hai, aur .size seedha milta hai. Aur bade data par add/delete tez hai.
lessons.why: Object shuru se hi "object" tha — key-value store nahi. Isliye usme numeric keys sort ho jaati hain, prototype se keys leak hoti hain, aur key sirf string ho sakti hai. Map aur Set asal mein usi kaam ke liye banaye gaye — isliye wo us kaam mein har tarah se behtar hain.

Map — object keys aur pakka order.
pros: Keys kuch bhi ho sakti hain.
Order pakka, size seedha.
Bade data par add/delete/lookup tez.
cons: JSON.stringify mein Map/Set khaali ho jaate hain.
Property access syntax nahi (m.a nahi chalta).
Chhote fixed data ke liye object hi simple hai.
gotchas: JSON.stringify(new Map()) "{}" deta hai — data gayab. [...map] convert karke bhejo.
Set object reference se compare karta hai — new Set([{a:1},{a:1}]) ki size 2 hai.
Object mein number-jaisi keys apne aap sort ho jaati hain — order chahiye to Map use karo.

lessons.name: JSON — parse, stringify, revivers, replacers, toJSON
lessons.desc: JSON.parse with reviver function for custom deserialization. JSON.stringify with replacer for filtering/formatting. toJSON method on objects for custom serialization. JSON.stringify loses functions, undefined, Symbol, Infinity, Date (to string).
lessons.q: What does JSON.stringify lose? How do you serialize a Date object properly?
lessons.qsub: What is a reviver function in JSON.parse? How do you implement custom serialization with toJSON?
terms: Convert karte waqt beech mein value badalne wala function.
lessons.what: Do methods, par unke chhupe hue niyam hi asli sawaal hain — kyunki JSON JavaScript ke saare types support nahi karta.
lessons.why: Har API call, har localStorage write isse hokar jaati hai. Par JSON JavaScript ke saare types support nahi karta — aur jo cheezein chup-chaap gayab ho jaati hain (Date, undefined, Map) wahi sabse aam bug banti hain. Isliye "kya survive nahi karta" jaanna zaroori hai.
where: Sirf string rakhta hai — JSON zaroori.
replacer se password/token hatana log bhejne se pehle.
pros: Har jagah chalta hai, koi library nahi chahiye.
replacer/reviver se poora control.
toJSON se class apna format tay kar sakti hai.
cons: Date, Map, Set, BigInt, undefined — kuch bhi survive nahi karta.
Circular reference par crash.
Bade objects par sync aur slow — main thread block.
gotchas: Deep clone ke liye JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) mat use karo — Date string ban jaati hai, undefined gayab. structuredClone() use karo.
Circular reference par stringify throw karta hai.
JSON.parse hamesha try/catch mein — bahar se aaya data kabhi bhi galat ho sakta hai.

lessons.name: Scope (Global / Function / Block)
lessons.desc: Scope determines where variables are visible. JS has global, function, and block scopes.
lessons.q: Explain the three types of scope in JavaScript with examples.
lessons.qsub: What is scope chain lookup and how does it work at runtime?
terms: Wo ilaaka jahan ek variable dikhta hai.
Variable na mile to JS bahar wale scope mein dhundta hai — global tak.
Scope ka faisla code likhne ki jagah se hota hai, chalane ki jagah se nahi.
lessons.what:
Teen tarah ke ilaake hote hain: global (poori file), function (ek function ke andar), aur block (ek { } ke andar — sirf let/const ke liye).

Jab JS ko koi variable chahiye, wo andar se bahar ki taraf dhundhta hai — apne scope mein, phir uske bahar wale mein, phir global tak. Ise scope chain kehte hain.
lessons.analogy: Ghar mein cheez dhundhna: pehle apne kamre mein, na mile to hall mein, na mile to poore ghar mein. Ulta nahi hota — hall se koi aapke kamre ki almari nahi khol sakta.
lessons.why: Iske bina har variable global hota aur do functions ke variable aapas mein takra jaate. Scope hi wo cheez hai jo closures ko mumkin banati hai — aur usi se this, hoisting aur module pattern sab nikalte hain.

Alag functions ek hi naam ka variable use kar sakte hain, koi jhagda nahi.
Sab kuch ek function ke andar rakh kar global ko saaf rakha jaata hai.
pros: Variables takrate nahi — har function ka apna ilaaka.
Block scope se for loop aur if ke variable leak nahi karte.
Global namespace saaf rehta hai.
cons: Deep nesting mein "ye variable aaya kahan se" dhundhna mushkil.
Scope chain lambi ho to lookup thoda slow (practically na ke barabar).
var ka function-scope aaj bhi purane code mein confusion deta hai.
gotchas: Lexical ka matlab: scope likhne ki jagah se tay hota hai, bulane ki jagah se nahi.
var block scope nahi maanta — if ke andar bhi poore function mein dikhta hai.
Bina let/const/var ke variable banane par wo global ban jaata hai (strict mode mein error).

lessons.name: Hoisting
lessons.desc: JS moves declarations (not initializations) to the top of their scope before execution.
lessons.q: What is hoisting? How does it behave differently for var vs let/const vs functions?
lessons.qsub: What is the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)?
terms: Chalne se pehle JS saari declarations ko upar utha leta hai — value ko nahi.
Temporal Dead Zone — block ke shuru se declaration tak ka wo hissa jahan let/const ko chhoo nahi sakte.
lessons.what:
Code chalne se pehle JS ek baar poora scan karta hai aur saare declarations note kar leta hai. Par value wahin par set hoti hai jahan likhi hai.

Isliye var declare se pehle use karne par undefined milta hai — variable exist karta hai, par value nahi aayi.
lessons.analogy: Class mein attendance register pehle ban jaata hai (sab naam likhe hain), par bachche apne time par aate hain. Naam register mein hai = declaration. Bachcha aaya nahi = value undefined.
lessons.why: var ka undefined dena bugs banata tha — code chal jaata tha par galat. Isliye let/const ne TDZ laaya: declare se pehle chhuo to error milega. Bug chhupne ki jagah turant dikhega.

Function declaration niche likhkar bhi upar bula sakte ho — helper functions ke liye aam.

pros: Function declarations niche likh kar bhi upar use kar sakte ho.
TDZ galtiyan chhupne nahi deta — turant error milta hai.
Code padhne ka order zaroori nahi rehta.
cons: var ka undefined silent bug banata hai.
Arrow function aur function expression hoist nahi hote — confusion hoti hai.
Beginners ke liye ye behaviour ulta lagta hai.
gotchas: Sirf declaration hoist hota hai, assignment nahi. Yahi poori cheez ka nichod hai.
function f(){} poora hoist hota hai, par var f = function(){} sirf var f tak.
class bhi TDZ mein hoti hai — declare se pehle new nahi kar sakte.

lessons.name: Execution Context & Call Stack
lessons.desc: JS creates a context for every function call; the call stack tracks the current execution chain.
lessons.q: What is an execution context? What gets created when a function is invoked?
lessons.qsub: Walk me through what happens step-by-step when this code runs: function a(){ b() } function b(){} a()
terms: Ek dabba jo batata hai: abhi kaunsa code chal raha hai, uske variables kya hain, aur this kya hai.
In dabbon ki dher. Sabse upar wala abhi chal raha hai.
lessons.what:
Jab bhi koi function chalta hai, JS uske liye ek naya dabba banata hai — usme us function ke variables, uska scope chain, aur uska this rehta hai.

Ye dabbe ek dher (stack) mein lagte hain. Sabse upar wala chal raha hota hai; wo khatam hote hi hat jaata hai aur neeche wala aage badhta hai.
lessons.analogy: Table par kitaabein rakhna. Nayi kitaab hamesha upar rakhi jaati hai aur upar se hi uthai jaati hai. Beech se nahi nikaal sakte.
lessons.why: Stack trace jo error mein dikhta hai — wo yahi dher hai. Aur "Maximum call stack size exceeded" ka matlab hai ki dher itni oonchi ho gayi ki gir gayi (infinite recursion).

Har recursive call ek naya dabba banati hai — isliye depth limit hoti hai.

pros: Order hamesha predictable hai — koi race condition nahi.
Stack trace se bug tak seedha pahuncha ja sakta hai.
Memory apne aap free ho jaati hai jab dabba hatta hai.

Bhaari function poore page ko block kar deta hai.
Async code stack trace todta hai — debugging mushkil.
gotchas: "Maximum call stack size exceeded" ka matlab hamesha infinite recursion hota hai — base case check karo.
Stack trace ulta padha jaata hai — sabse upar wali line sabse aakhir mein chali thi.
Recursion ki jagah loop use karne se stack limit ki problem khatam ho jaati hai.

lessons.name: Closures
lessons.desc: A function that "remembers" variables from its outer scope even after that scope has returned.
lessons.q: What is a closure? Give a real-world use case and a common pitfall.
lessons.qsub: How does the classic loop-with-setTimeout bug demonstrate closures? How do you fix it?
terms: Wo ilaaka jahan ek variable dikhta hai.
Ek function jo apne bahar wale variables yaad rakhta hai — bahar wala function khatam hone ke baad bhi.
lessons.what:
Function ke andar function banao, to andar wale ko bahar wale ke variables dikhte hain. Ye normal hai.

Kamaal ye hai: bahar wala khatam ho jaane ke baad bhi andar wala un variables ko yaad rakhta hai. Wo mitte nahi. Usi ko closure kehte hain.
lessons.analogy: Office se ghar jaate waqt ek file bag mein daal li. Office band ho gaya — par file abhi bhi bag mein hai. Function = aap, bag = closure.
lessons.why: JavaScript mein private jaisa kuch tha hi nahi. To data aisa kaise banayein jise sirf kuch functions chhoo sakein? Closure ne wo hal diya — variable andar rakho, bahar sirf zaroori functions do.

where: useState closure par khada hai — har component apna state yaad rakhta hai.
Timer ka id closure mein rehta hai, isliye har debounce ka apna timer hota hai.
Module pattern — secret ko bahar se koi nahi chhoo sakta.
pros: Asli private data — JS mein iske alawa tarika hi nahi tha.
Har call par naya, alag bag — do counters ek doosre ko nahi chhedte.
Global variables ki zarurat khatam.
cons: Memory nahi chhodta jab tak closure zinda hai.
Loop + var ke saath classic bug (neeche).
Zyada nesting padhne mein bhaari.
gotchas: for (var i=0;i<3;i++) setTimeout(()=>log(i)) teeno baar 3 deta hai — var ek hi variable hai. let use karo.

Interview mein sirf definition mat dena — ek asli use (debounce/useState) bhi batao.

lessons.name: IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expression)
lessons.desc: A function that runs the moment it is defined — used to create isolated scope.
lessons.q: What is an IIFE? Why was it heavily used before ES6 modules?
lessons.qsub: How does an IIFE prevent polluting the global scope?
terms: Immediately Invoked Function Expression — banate hi turant chalne wala function.
Apna alag ilaaka taaki naam global mein na takraayein.
lessons.what:
Ek function jo likhte hi turant chal jaata hai: (function(){ ... })().

Uska ek hi maqsad tha — ek apna scope bana lena, taaki andar ke variables global mein na jaayein.
lessons.why:
let/const aur ES modules se pehle, scope banane ka ek hi tarika tha: function. To log poore file ko ek function mein lapet dete the.

Aaj iski zarurat lagbhag khatam hai — block scope aur modules ne ye kaam le liya. Par purane code aur library bundles mein ye har jagah milega, isliye pehchanna zaroori hai.
where: jQuery-era libraries poori tarah IIFE mein lipti hoti thin.
Webpack/Rollup ka output aaj bhi IIFE mein lapeta jaata hai.
Private data + public API — closure ke saath milkar.
pros: Global namespace saaf rakhta hai.
Ek baar ka setup code chalane ka saaf tarika.
Closure ke saath private data deta hai.
cons: Aaj lagbhag zarurat nahi — let/block/modules kaafi hain.
Syntax padhne mein bhaari lagta hai.
Bina naam ke function debugging mein "anonymous" dikhta hai.
gotchas: Pichhli line semicolon se khatam nahi hui to IIFE ka ( use function call samajh liya jaata hai — ASI ka classic bug.
Aaj naye code mein IIFE likhne ki zarurat nahi — interview mein ye bata dena achha signal hai.
IIFE khud private data nahi deta — wo closure deta hai. IIFE sirf scope banata hai.

lessons.name: Arrow Functions
lessons.desc: Concise function syntax that lexically binds this and cannot be used as constructors.
lessons.q: How are arrow functions different from regular functions? List at least 3 differences.
lessons.qsub: Why can't arrow functions be used as constructors or generators?
terms: Chhota syntax — aur uska apna this, arguments nahi hota.
Curly braces na ho to value apne aap return ho jaati hai.
lessons.what:
Arrow function sirf chhota syntax nahi hai. Uske paas apna this hota hi nahi — wo jahan likha gaya hai, wahan ka this udhaar leta hai.

Isi ek farak se tay hota hai ki kab arrow use karna hai aur kab nahi.
lessons.why: Pehle callback ke andar this kho jaata tha, to log const self = this likhte the ya .bind(this) lagate the. Arrow ne wo jhanjhat poori tarah khatam kar diya.
where: map, filter, reduce — chhota syntax yahan sabse zyada kaam aata hai.
setTimeout, promise .then — bahar ka this apne aap mil jaata hai.
Event handlers arrow se likho to bind karne ki zarurat nahi padti.
pros: Callback ke andar this apne aap sahi rehta hai.
Chhota syntax — map/filter padhne mein saaf.
Implicit return se ek-line functions bahut chhote ho jaate hain.
cons: Object method ke liye galat — this object ko point nahi karta.
Constructor nahi ban sakta, arguments nahi milta.
Bahut chhota likhne ke chakkar mein code padhna mushkil ho jaata hai.
gotchas: Object literal return karne ke liye bracket lagao: () => ({ a: 1 }). Bina bracket ke wo block samjha jaata hai.
Arrow ka this .call()/.bind() se bhi nahi badla ja sakta.
Prototype par method arrow se mat likho — wahan normal function chahiye.

lessons.name: this Keyword
lessons.desc: this refers to the object that is executing the current function — its value depends on call context.
lessons.q: Explain how this is determined. What are the four rules of binding?
lessons.qsub: What does this refer to inside an arrow function? Why is that useful in React?
terms: Wo object jispe function abhi chal raha hai.
Wo jagah jahan se function bulaya gaya — yahi this tay karta hai.
lessons.what:
this ki value function likhne se tay nahi hoti — bulane se tay hoti hai. Yahi ek line poora confusion khatam kar deti hai.

Ek hi function alag jagah se bulane par alag this dega.
lessons.analogy: "Main" shabd jaisa. Kaun bol raha hai uspe matlab badal jaata hai — shabd wahi hai. this bhi wahi hai: kaun bula raha hai, uspe value badalti hai.
lessons.why: Ek hi method ko hazaar objects share karte hain — method ka code ek jagah hota hai. To method ko batana padta hai ki wo kis object ka data use kare. Wo jawab this hai.

Method ko callback ki tarah pass karo to this kho jaata hai — arrow ya .bind() chahiye.
addEventListener mein normal function ka this = wo element hota hai.
pros: Ek method ka code hazaar objects share kar sakte hain.
Arrow function ne callback wala this problem lagbhag khatam kar diya.
call/apply/bind se this par poora control milta hai.
cons: Value bulane par tay hoti hai — padh kar guess karna mushkil.
Method ko variable mein daalte hi this toot jaata hai.
Arrow aur normal function ka behaviour ulta hai — confusion aam hai.
gotchas: Arrow function ka apna this hota hi nahi — wo jahan likha hai wahan ka udhaar leta hai. Isliye object method ke liye arrow mat use karo.
const fn = obj.method; fn() — this khो gaya. Ye sabse aam bug hai.
Interview mein 4 niyam ki list (new → call/bind → dot → akela) bata dena — wahi poora jawab hai.

lessons.name: call / apply / bind
lessons.desc: Methods to explicitly set this for a function call. bind returns a new function; call/apply invoke immediately.
lessons.q: What is the difference between call, apply, and bind? Implement bind from scratch.
lessons.qsub: When would you use bind over an arrow function?
terms: this aur arguments alag-alag do, turant chalao.
Turant nahi chalata — ek naya function deta hai jiska this fix ho gaya.
lessons.what:
Teeno ek hi kaam ke liye hain: this khud tay karna.

call aur apply function ko turant chalate hain (bas arguments dene ka tarika alag hai). bind chalata nahi — wo ek naya function deta hai jiska this hamesha ke liye fix ho gaya.
lessons.why: Ye teeno tab chahiye jab this apne aap sahi nahi aa raha ho. Sabse aam jagah: method ko callback ki tarah kisi aur ko de dena — wahan this toot jaata hai, aur bind use jod kar rakhta hai. Aur doosri jagah: kisi aur object ka method udhaar lena.

Array method ko array-jaisi cheez par chalana: [].slice.call(arguments).
Function.prototype.bind khud likhna machine coding ka classic sawaal hai.
pros: this par poora control.
bind se arguments bhi pehle se bhar sakte ho (partial application).
Doosre object ka method udhaar le sakte ho.
cons: bind har baar naya function banata hai — loop mein mehnga.
Bound function ko dobara bind nahi kar sakte.
Arrow function par teeno ka this par koi asar nahi hota.
gotchas: Yaad rakhne ka tarika: call = comma se arguments, apply = array, bind = baad mein.
React mein onClick={this.fn.bind(this)} har render par naya function banata hai — arrow ya constructor mein bind karo.
bind arrow function par kaam nahi karta — uska this badla hi nahi ja sakta.

lessons.name: Higher-Order Functions
lessons.desc: Functions that take other functions as arguments or return them — the basis of functional JS.
lessons.q: What is a higher-order function? Implement map, filter, and reduce from scratch.
lessons.qsub: What is function composition and how does it differ from currying?
terms: Aisa function jo doosra function leta hai ya lautata hai.
Wo function jo aap kisi aur function ko de dete ho ki "ise chala lena".
lessons.what:
JavaScript mein function ek normal value hai — use variable mein rakh sakte ho, argument mein bhej sakte ho, return kar sakte ho.

Jo function doosre function ko leta ya lautata hai, use higher-order function kehte hain. map, filter, setTimeout, addEventListener — sab yahi hain.
lessons.why: Iske bina aapko har chhoti cheez ke liye poora loop likhna padta. HOF se "kya karna hai" aur "kaise ghoomna hai" alag ho jaate hain — aur wahi code ko chhota aur padhne layak banata hai.
where: map/filter/reduce — API se aaye data ko shape dene ka standard tarika.
List render karna poora map par khada hai.
debounce, once, memoize — sab function lete aur lautate hain.
pros: Loop ka boilerplate khatam — iraada seedha dikhta hai.
Chain kar sakte ho, har step alag se test ho sakta hai.
Reusable — ek hi map har tarah ke data par chalta hai.
cons: Har chain ek naya array banati hai — bahut bade data par memory kharch.
Zyada chaining padhne mein bhaari ho jaati hai.
Plain for loop bade data par thoda tez hota hai.
gotchas: map hamesha naya array deta hai — sirf side-effect ke liye forEach use karo.
reduce mein initial value dena bhoolna khaali array par error deta hai: reduce(fn, 0).
forEach se break nahi kar sakte — uske liye for...of ya some() chahiye.

lessons.name: Currying & Partial Application
lessons.desc: Transforming a multi-argument function into a sequence of single-argument functions.
lessons.q: Explain currying. Write a curry function that works for any number of arguments.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between currying and partial application?
terms: Ek function jo kai arguments leta tha, use ek-ek argument lene wale functions ki chain mein todna.
Kuch arguments abhi de dena, baaki baad mein.
lessons.what:
add(a, b, c) ko add(a)(b)(c) bana dena — yahi currying hai.

Faayda ye hai ki aap kuch arguments pehle bhar kar ek naya, chhota function bana sakte ho.
lessons.analogy: Chai ka order: "ek chai, kam cheeni, adrak wali". Currying matlab pehle bol do "kam cheeni, adrak wali" — ab har baar sirf "ek chai" bolna kaafi hai.
lessons.why: Jab ek hi setting baar-baar repeat ho rahi ho, to use ek baar bhar kar ek naya function bana lo. Code se duplication hat jaati hai.
where: API base URL, log level, headers — ek baar bharo, baar-baar use karo.
onDelete(id) — id pehle bind karke handler bana lo.
curry(fn) khud implement karna machine coding ka classic sawaal hai.
pros: Repeat hone wale arguments ek baar bhar do.
Chhote, specific functions bana kar naam de sakte ho.
Compose karne mein aasan.
cons: f(a)(b)(c) padhne mein ajeeb lagta hai.
Har step ek naya function banata hai — thoda overhead.
Debugging mushkil — stack mein anonymous functions dikhte hain.
gotchas: Currying aur partial application ek nahi hain: currying hamesha ek-ek argument leti hai, partial application kitne bhi.
Aksar ek simple wrapper function currying se zyada padhne layak hota hai — zabardasti mat karo.
Generic curry(fn) likhne ke liye fn.length se argument count nikalna padta hai.

lessons.name: Memoization
lessons.desc: Caching the result of expensive function calls so repeated calls with the same input are fast.
lessons.q: Implement a generic memoize function. What are its tradeoffs?
lessons.qsub: How does React.memo / useMemo relate to this concept?
terms: Function ke jawab ko yaad rakh lena, taaki wahi input dobara aaye to dobara calculate na karna pade.
Wo jagah jahan purane jawab rakhe jaate hain.
Wahi input → hamesha wahi output, aur duniya mein kuch na badle.
lessons.what:
Agar ek function bhaari hai aur wahi input baar-baar aata hai, to har baar calculate karna barbaadi hai.

Jawab ek cache (aksar Map) mein rakh lo. Agli baar wahi input aaye to seedha wahan se de do.
lessons.analogy: Calculator par 17 × 23 bar-bar lagana. Ek baar nikaal kar diary mein likh lo — agli baar diary dekh lo, dobara mat lagao.
lessons.why: Ye tabhi kaam karta hai jab function pure ho — yaani wahi input hamesha wahi output de. Agar function har baar alag jawab de sakta hai (jaise API call ya random), to purana jawab dena galat hoga.
where: Fibonacci, DP problems — exponential se linear ho jaata hai.
useMemo aur React.memo yahi soch hai — render dobara mat karo.
memoize(fn) likhna machine coding mein aksar poocha jaata hai.
pros: Repeat calculation par bahut bada speed faayda.
Recursion ko exponential se linear bana deta hai.
Function ka code badalna nahi padta — bas wrap kar do.
cons: Memory kharch karta hai — cache badhta rehta hai.
Sirf pure functions par safe hai.
Object arguments ke liye key banana mushkil aur slow.
gotchas: JSON.stringify se key banana object key order par depend karta hai aur bada data par slow hai.
Cache kabhi khaali nahi hota to wo memory leak ban jaata hai — size limit ya WeakMap use karo.
Impure function (API call, Date.now(), random) ko memoize karna bug hai, optimization nahi.

lessons.name: Prototype Chain
lessons.desc: Every JS object has a hidden __proto__ link forming a chain up to Object.prototype for property lookup.
lessons.q: Explain the prototype chain. How does property lookup work in JavaScript?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between __proto__ and prototype?
terms: Ek object jispe doosre object apne "na mile to yahan dekho" ka pata rakhte hain.
Object ka apne prototype tak ka link.
Function ki wo property jo new se bane objects ka prototype banti hai.
lessons.what:
JS mein har object ke paas ek chhupa hua link hota hai — apne prototype tak. Jab aap obj.foo maangte ho aur wo object par nahi hai, JS us link par chala jaata hai. Wahan bhi nahi mila to aur upar. null tak.

Isi chain ko prototype chain kehte hain. Yahi JS ka inheritance hai.
lessons.analogy: Ghar mein cheez na mile to padosi se maang lena, wahan na mile to uske padosi se. Aur ek jagah aisi aati hai jahan aage koi nahi (null) — tab undefined.
lessons.why: Isi wajah se har array ke paas map hota hai bina uske andar likhe. map Array.prototype par ek hi jagah rehta hai — hazaar arrays usi ko share karte hain. Memory bachti hai.

DevTools mein [[Prototype]] khol kar dekhoge to poori chain dikhti hai.
pros: Methods ek hi jagah — hazaar objects share karte hain, memory bachti hai.
Chalte waqt bhi behaviour add kiya ja sakta hai.
Class-based inheritance se zyada flexible.
cons: Lambi chain lookup thoda slow karti hai.
Built-in prototype badalna (monkey-patching) khatarnak hai.
Class-based languages se aane walon ko confusing lagta hai.
gotchas: __proto__ aur prototype alag hain: __proto__ object par hota hai, prototype function par.
for...in viraasat mein mili properties bhi ghoomta hai — Object.keys() nahi.
Array.prototype mein apna method mat jodo — har array par aa jaayega aur libraries toot sakti hain.

lessons.name: new Keyword
lessons.desc: Creates a blank object, sets its prototype, runs the constructor with this, and returns the object.
lessons.q: What does the new keyword do step by step? What happens if a constructor returns an object?
lessons.qsub: What happens if you call a constructor without new?
terms: Function ko constructor ki tarah chalata hai aur naya object banata hai.
Wo function jo new ke saath bulaya jaata hai.
lessons.what:
new Foo() lagane par JS chaar cheezein karta hai, ussi order mein:

1. Ek khaali object banata hai.
2. Us object ka prototype Foo.prototype set karta hai.
3. Foo ko chalata hai jisme this = wo naya object.
4. Object return karta hai (jab tak function khud koi object return na kare).
lessons.why: Ye chaar kadam jaanna isliye zaroori hai kyunki har bug inhi se samajh aata hai. new bhoolne par this galat kyu ho jaata hai, prototype kaise judta hai, aur constructor se object return karne par kya hota hai — teeno ka jawab isi list mein hai. Interview mein ye seedha poocha jaata hai.

"new andar se kya karta hai" seedha poocha jaata hai — chaar steps bata do.
pros: Ek hi tarika, har jagah same — objects banane ka standard.
Prototype apne aap jud jaata hai.
new.target se galat use pakad sakte ho.
cons: new bhoolna chup-chaap bug banata hai (non-strict mein).
Constructor se object return karna behaviour badal deta hai — confusing.
Arrow functions ke saath kaam hi nahi karta.
gotchas: Constructor se object return karo to wo this ko override kar deta hai. Primitive return karo to ignore ho jaata hai.
Class ko new ke bina bulana hamesha error deta hai — constructor function chup-chaap chal jaata hai.
Arrow function par new nahi laga sakte — uske paas prototype hota hi nahi.

lessons.name: ES6 Classes
lessons.desc: Syntactic sugar over prototype-based inheritance — classes don't add new OOP semantics, just cleaner syntax.
lessons.q: Are JavaScript classes "real" classes? What is happening under the hood?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between a class expression and declaration? What are static methods?
terms: Prototype-based inheritance ka saaf syntax. Andar prototypes hi chalte hain.
Naya kaam nahi, purane kaam ka behtar likhne ka tarika.
Asli private field — bahar se chhua hi nahi ja sakta.
lessons.what:
class JavaScript mein koi nayi cheez nahi laayi. Wo wahi prototype chain hai, bas likhne ka tarika saaf ho gaya.

class Dog { bark(){} } asal mein Dog.prototype.bark hi banata hai.
lessons.why: Prototype wala purana syntax (Dog.prototype.bark = function...) padhne mein bikhra hua tha aur inheritance set karna 4-5 line ka jugaad tha. class ne wo saaf kar diya — aur # private fields jaisa naya faayda bhi diya jo pehle sirf closure se milta tha.
where: Data ke saath uske niyam ek jagah — validation, computed values.
class ApiError extends Error — sabse aam asli use.
pros: Prototype wale jugaad se kahin saaf syntax.
# se asli private fields milte hain.
extends/super se inheritance seedha.
cons: Log samajhte hain ki ye Java jaisi class hai — hai nahi, andar prototype hai.
JS mein aksar plain objects + functions kaafi hote hain.
Deep hierarchy JS mein aur bhi jaldi bhaari ho jaati hai.
gotchas: Class hoist hoti hai par TDZ mein rehti hai — declare se pehle new nahi kar sakte.
Class ka code hamesha strict mode mein chalta hai, chahe aapne "use strict" na likha ho.
Method ko variable mein daalte hi this kho jaata hai — arrow class field (fn = () => {}) se bachо.

lessons.name: Prototypal vs Classical Inheritance
lessons.desc: JS uses object-to-object delegation, not class-to-instance. extends sets up the prototype chain.
lessons.q: Explain the difference between prototypal and classical inheritance. When is composition better?
lessons.qsub: Implement Object.create from scratch.
terms: Object seedha doosre object se cheezein leta hai.
Class se class — Java/C++ wala tarika. JS mein ye asli nahi hai.
Inheritance ki jagah cheezein jod kar banana.
lessons.what:
Java mein class ek blueprint hai aur objects usse bante hain. JS mein object seedha doosre object se cheezein leta hai — koi blueprint beech mein nahi.

class ... extends Java jaisa dikhta hai, par andar wahi prototype linking chal rahi hoti hai.
lessons.why:
Farak samajhna isliye zaroori hai kyunki JS mein aap chalte waqt bhi prototype badal sakte ho, aur ek object ko doosre object se seedha bana sakte ho — Java mein ye mumkin hi nahi.

Aur practical salah: JS mein deep inheritance se bacho. Composition (cheezein jodna) aksar behtar hai.
where: extends Error — inheritance ka sabse saaf, sabse aam use.
React.Component, custom HTML elements — inheritance zaroori hai.
Mixins/composition — jab kai jagah se behaviour chahiye.
pros: Chalte waqt bhi prototype badla ja sakta hai.
Object se seedha object bana sakte ho — bina class ke.
Composition ke saath milakar bahut flexible.
cons: Deep chain padhna aur debug karna mushkil.
Ek hi baap — do jagah se code chahiye to composition hi raasta.
setPrototypeOf chalte waqt use karna performance kharab karta hai.
gotchas: extends ke saath super() sabse pehle — this use karne se pehle.
Object.create(null) se aisa object banta hai jiska koi prototype nahi — pure dictionary ke liye best.
Interview mein: "JS mein classical inheritance hai hi nahi, wo prototypal par syntax sugar hai" — ye jawab strong hai.

lessons.name: Object.create / assign / freeze / seal
lessons.desc: Built-in methods to create, copy, and lock down objects at the property descriptor level.
lessons.q: What is the difference between Object.freeze and Object.seal? When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: Does Object.freeze do a deep freeze? How would you implement deep freeze?
terms: Diye hue prototype ke saath naya object.
Ek object mein doosre ki properties copy (shallow).
freeze = kuch bhi mat badlo. seal = nayi mat jodo, purani badal sakte ho.
lessons.what: Chaar utility jo objects ke saath roz kaam aati hain — aur teeno freeze/seal wale sirf upar ke level par kaam karte hain.
lessons.why: Ye char utility roz kaam aati hain — par inka shallow hona hi sabse bada trap hai. Log Object.freeze laga kar samajh lete hain ki poora object safe hai, jabki andar wala nested object abhi bhi badla ja sakta hai. Isliye inhe use karne se pehle unki seema jaanna zaroori hai.
where: Object.freeze se config galti se badle nahi.
pros: Spread se merge padhne mein bahut saaf.
freeze galti se hone wale badlav rok deta hai.
entries/fromEntries se object par map/filter chala sakte ho.
cons: freeze aur assign dono shallow hain — andar ka bacha nahi.
Non-strict mode mein frozen object par likhna chup-chaap ignore hota hai.
freeze bade objects par thoda mehnga hai.
gotchas: Object.freeze shallow hai — nested object abhi bhi badla ja sakta hai. Deep freeze khud likhna padta hai.
Object.assign getters ko chala deta hai aur value copy kar leta hai — getter copy nahi hota.
Object.create(null) wale object par toString, hasOwnProperty kuch nahi hota.

lessons.name: Mixins & Composition
lessons.desc: Combining functionality from multiple sources without inheritance — prefer composition over inheritance.
lessons.q: What is a mixin in JavaScript? How does it solve the diamond problem of multiple inheritance?
lessons.qsub: When would you choose composition over inheritance?
terms: Behaviour ka ek tukda jise kai classes/objects mein mila diya jaaye.
Inheritance ki jagah cheezein jod kar banana.
lessons.what:
JS mein ek class ka ek hi baap ho sakta hai. Par aksar behaviour do-teen jagah se chahiye hota hai.

Mixin uska jugaad hai: behaviour ko ek plain object ya function mein rakho, aur jise chahiye usme mila do.
lessons.why: Inheritance ka classic dard: ElectricCar, FlyingCar, ElectricFlyingCar... har combination ki apni class. Mixin se combination banana jodne jaisa ho jaata hai, nayi class banane jaisa nahi.
where: Logging, serialization, events — kai classes ko chahiye.
Mixins uska core feature tha (Vue 3 mein composition API ne le liya).
Ek class ko event-emitter banana bina inheritance ke.
pros: Ek baap ki limit se bachaata hai.
Combination banana sasta — nayi class nahi banani padti.
Chhote, alag-alag tukde — test karna aasan.
cons: Naam takra sakte hain — do mixins mein ek hi method ho to chup-chaap ek overwrite ho jaata hai.
"Ye method aaya kahan se?" dhundhna mushkil.
Zyada mixins se class ka behaviour bikhar jaata hai.
gotchas: Object.assign(Class.prototype, mixin) chup-chaap purani method overwrite kar deta hai — koi warning nahi.
Mixin mein state (fields) rakhna khatarnak hai — sab instances share kar sakte hain.
Aksar simple composition (field mein object rakhna) mixin se saaf hota hai — pehle wo sochо.

lessons.name: Symbol & Well-Known Symbols
lessons.desc: Unique, non-string primitive used as private(-ish) object keys; well-known symbols customize language behaviour.
lessons.q: What problem does Symbol solve? What is Symbol.iterator and how do you use it?
lessons.qsub: How can you use Symbol.toPrimitive to control type coercion on custom objects?
terms: Ek hamesha-unique value. Do symbols kabhi barabar nahi hote.
JS ke apne symbols jo language ke behaviour ko hook karte hain.
lessons.what:
Symbol("id") har baar ek bilkul nayi value deta hai — chahe naam same ho. Isliye object key ke liye ye kabhi takra nahi sakta.

Aur JS ke apne kuch symbols hain (Symbol.iterator jaise) jinse aap language ka behaviour badal sakte ho.
lessons.why: Do kaam: (1) kisi doosre ke object mein apni property jodni ho bina uski keys se takraye. (2) Apne object ko for...of, spread, destructuring ke layak banana — Symbol.iterator se.
where: User ke object mein apna data jodna bina takrav ke.
Symbol.iterator se apni class for...of mein chalti hai.
React, Vue apne internal flags symbols se rakhte hain.
pros: Key kabhi takrati nahi — 100% unique.
Object.keys/JSON se chhupi rehti hai.
Well-known symbols se language ka behaviour customize kar sakte ho.
cons: Kam use hota hai — team mein sab nahi jaante.
Debug karna mushkil — console mein Symbol(id) hi dikhta hai.
JSON.stringify mein gayab ho jaata hai (kabhi ye achha hai, kabhi bug).
gotchas: Symbol key private nahi hai — Object.getOwnPropertySymbols() se mil jaati hai. Wo sirf chhupi hai.
Symbol.for("x") global registry se leta hai — wahi symbol dobara milta hai. Symbol("x") hamesha naya.
Symbol ko string mein apne aap convert nahi kar sakte — String(sym) likhna padta hai.

lessons.name: Iterable & Iterator Protocol
lessons.desc: Any object with [Symbol.iterator] is iterable; the iterator protocol defines how values are produced one by one.
lessons.q: What is the iterator protocol? How do you make a custom object work with for...of?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between an iterable and an iterator?
terms: Aisi cheez jispe for...of chal sake — usme Symbol.iterator hota hai.
Wo cheez jiske paas next() ho jo {value, done} lautaye.
lessons.what:
for...of, spread (...), destructuring — ye sab ek hi cheez par khade hain: iterable protocol.

Koi bhi object jisme [Symbol.iterator]() ho, ye sab kuch apne aap kaam karne lagta hai.
lessons.why: Isi ki wajah se Array, String, Map, Set, NodeList — sab par ek hi tarah for...of chalta hai. Aur aap apni class ko bhi wahi behaviour de sakte ho, ek method likh kar.
where: Users ko spread/destructuring ka faayda dena.
pros: Ek method se spread, for...of, destructuring sab mil jaate hain.
Generator se likhna 2 line ka kaam.
Lazy ho sakta hai — poora data banane ki zarurat nahi.
cons: Manual iterator likhna verbose hai.
Ek baar khatam hone par dobara nahi chalta.
Bahut bade data par har next() ka thoda overhead.
gotchas: for...in keys deta hai (aur inherited bhi), for...of values. Array par hamesha for...of.
Plain object iterable nahi hai — Object.entries() use karo.
Generator (*[Symbol.iterator]) manual iterator se hamesha aasan hai.

lessons.name: Generators & Iterators
lessons.desc: Functions that can pause and resume execution using yield — the foundation of async/await internals.
lessons.q: What is a generator function? What problem does it solve? How does it relate to async/await?
lessons.qsub: Implement an infinite Fibonacci sequence using a generator.
terms: Aisa function jo beech mein ruk sakta hai aur baad mein wahin se aage badh sakta hai.
Wo jagah jahan function rukta hai aur ek value bahar deta hai.
Ek cheez jiske paas next() ho jo {value, done} lautaye.
lessons.what:
Normal function ek baar chala to poora chal kar hi rukta hai. Generator (function*) beech mein ruk sakta hai — yield par.

Aur sabse kaam ki baat: ruka hua kaun rakhta hai? Bahar wala. Aap next() bulao, tabhi wo aage badhega.
lessons.analogy: Netflix ki series. Ek episode dekha (yield), paused. Aap "next" dabao tabhi agla chalega. Poori series ek saath nahi chalti.
lessons.why: Do asli kaam: infinite ya bade sequences (poora array banaye bina ek-ek karke value dena), aur async/await ka andar ka mechanism — async/await asal mein generators + promises se hi bana hai.
where: Poora array banaye bina ek-ek record process karna.
ID generator, fibonacci — jitna chahiye utna hi banta hai.
Poora library generators par khada hai.
pros: Lazy — value tabhi banti hai jab maango. Memory bachti hai.
Infinite sequences mumkin.
Async/await ka andar samajhne ki chaabi.
cons: Syntax aam nahi hai — team mein sab nahi samajhte.
Zyadatar cases mein async/await hi kaafi hai.
Debugging mushkil — control aage-peeche kudta hai.
gotchas: function* bulane par code chalta nahi — sirf ek iterator milta hai. Pehla next() hi use chalata hai.
next(value) se aap andar value bhej bhi sakte ho — yield uska result ban jaata hai.
Generator ek baar khatam (done: true) ho gaya to dobara chalu nahi hota — naya banana padta hai.

lessons.name: Proxy & Reflect
lessons.desc: Proxy intercepts object operations (get, set, delete); Reflect provides default behaviour for those ops.
lessons.q: What can you do with Proxy that you cannot do otherwise? Give a real use case.
lessons.qsub: How does Vue 3's reactivity system use Proxy?
terms: Ek object ke aage khada pehredaar — har read/write use se hokar jaata hai.
Wo function jo kisi operation ko pakadta hai — get, set, has.
Default behaviour chalane ka saaf tarika — Reflect.get(...).
lessons.what:
Proxy ek object ke aage khada ho jaata hai. Ab koi bhi us object se kuch padhega ya likhega, wo pehle aapke paas aayega.

Aap wahan validation, logging, default values — kuch bhi laga sakte ho.
lessons.why: Yahi Vue 3 ki reactivity hai. state.count++ likhne par UI kaise update hota hai? Kyunki state ek Proxy hai aur set trap ne pakad liya ki kuch badla.
where: Poori reactivity Proxy par khadi hai.
Object par likhne se pehle rules check karna.
Test mein poore object ko intercept karna.
pros: Object ka behaviour badal sakte ho bina uska code chhue.
Reactivity ka sabse saaf tarika.
Reflect se default behaviour ek line mein.
cons: Normal object se slow hai — har access ek function call.
Debugging confusing — dikhta object hai, chal Proxy raha hai.
Polyfill nahi ho sakta — purane browsers mein bilkul nahi.
gotchas: Trap mein hamesha Reflect use karo — apne haath se default likhne par this aur edge cases galat ho jaate hain.
Proxy nested objects ko apne aap wrap nahi karta — deep reactivity khud banani padti hai.
proxy === target false hota hai — comparison mein ye trap kar sakta hai.

lessons.name: Try/Catch/Finally — error propagation, finally semantics
lessons.desc: try/catch/finally is JS error handling. catch blocks receive the error object. finally always runs (even after return). Errors propagate up the call stack if uncaught. throw can re-throw or throw new errors.
lessons.q: Explain try/catch/finally execution order. What happens if catch also throws?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between throw new Error() and just throw? When would you re-throw?
terms: Galti phenkna — code wahin ruk kar upar chala jaata hai.
Chahe kuch bhi ho — ye hamesha chalta hai.
Error upar ki taraf chadhta hai jab tak koi pakad na le.
lessons.what:
throw hone par function wahin ruk jaata hai aur error upar chadhta hai — jisne bulaya tha, uske paas. Wahan bhi catch na ho to aur upar. Kahin bhi na pakda jaaye to program crash.

finally hamesha chalta hai — error aaye ya na aaye, return ho jaaye tab bhi.
lessons.why: Cleanup ke liye finally hi sahi jagah hai — loader band karna, connection chhodna, lock hataana. Kyunki wo har raaste par chalta hai: normal, error, aur early return.
where: Bahar se aaya data kabhi bhi galat ho sakta hai.
pros: Error handling ek jagah — har call par check nahi karna.
finally se cleanup pakka hota hai.
Error apne aap upar chadhta hai — beech wale functions ko kuch nahi karna.
cons: Async callbacks ke errors nahi pakadta.
Bada try block chhupa deta hai ki asli error kahan se aayi.
Error nigal jaana (khaali catch) sabse khatarnak habit hai.
gotchas: setTimeout/callback ke andar ka throw bahar wale try/catch mein nahi pakda jaata.
finally mein return mat likho — wo try ka error aur return dono nigal jaata hai.
Khaali catch {} mat chhodo — kam se kam log karo, warna bug hamesha ke liye chhup jaata hai.

lessons.name: Error Types — TypeError, ReferenceError, SyntaxError, RangeError
lessons.desc: TypeError: wrong type (e.g. calling non-function). ReferenceError: undefined variable. SyntaxError: invalid code. RangeError: value out of range. Each has distinct causes and debugging approaches.
lessons.q: What is the difference between TypeError and ReferenceError? Give examples of each.
lessons.qsub: When might you encounter a RangeError? How do you debug "Maximum call stack size exceeded"?
terms: Value ka type galat — undefined par method bulana.
Aisa variable jo hai hi nahi.
Code likhne mein galti — chalne se pehle hi.
lessons.what: JS ke apne error types hain, aur error ka naam hi aadha jawab hota hai — kis tarah ki galti hui, wo turant bata deta hai.
lessons.why: Error ka naam hi aadha jawab hota hai. TypeError matlab value ka type galat tha; ReferenceError matlab wo cheez hai hi nahi. Ye farak jaanne se debugging ka waqt aadha ho jaata hai — aur instanceof se alag-alag errors ko alag tarah handle bhi kar sakte ho.
where: Error ka naam padh kar hi 50% jawab mil jaata hai.
instanceof se alag-alag error alag tarah handle.
Sentry jaise tools error type se group karte hain.
pros: Naam se turant pata chalta hai kya galat hua.
instanceof se saaf handling.
stack se seedha source tak.
cons: Minified production code mein stack padha nahi jaata (source maps chahiye).
Alag browsers ke messages alag hote hain.
SyntaxError chalne se pehle aata hai — try/catch se pakda nahi ja sakta.
gotchas: "Cannot read properties of undefined" ka matlab: dot se pehle wali cheez undefined hai — dot ke baad wali nahi.
SyntaxError try/catch se nahi pakda jaata (JSON.parse wala chhod kar) — wo parse time par aata hai.
Production mein stack samajhne ke liye source maps upload karna zaroori hai.

lessons.name: Custom Error Classes — extending Error, error codes
lessons.desc: Extend Error to create domain-specific errors (ValidationError, NotFoundError). Set name, message, and custom properties (statusCode, code). Enables typed catch blocks and better API error responses.
lessons.q: How do you create a custom error class in JavaScript? Why would you?
lessons.qsub: How do you preserve the stack trace when extending Error? What is the cause option in Error()?
terms: Asli wajah wale error ko naye error ke saath jodna.
lessons.what:
throw new Error("kuch galat") se caller ko sirf ek string milti hai — aur string se code faisla nahi kar sakta.

Apni Error class banao: ab caller instanceof se pehchan sakta hai, aur error apne saath data bhi le jaa sakta hai.
lessons.why: Plain Error se caller ko sirf ek string milti hai, aur string se code faisla nahi kar sakta. Aur agar aap message ka ek shabd badal do, to uspe likha hua if chup-chaap toot jaayega. Apni Error class se caller instanceof se pehchan sakta hai aur error apne saath data (kaunsa field, kaunsi id) le jaa sakta hai.
where: HTTP status ko domain errors mein badalna.
Kaunsa field galat hai, wo error ke saath.
pros: Caller instanceof se saaf faisla le sakta hai.
Error apne saath data le jaata hai (field, id, status).
Ek saanjha baap se poora parivaar ek catch mein.
cons: setPrototypeOf wala jugaad yaad rakhna padta hai.
Bahut error classes bana dena over-engineering hai.
Errors network par bhejte waqt serialize karna padta hai.
gotchas: Object.setPrototypeOf(this, new.target.prototype) zaroori hai — bina iske instanceof kuch targets par false deta hai.
this.name set karo, warna stack mein hamesha "Error" dikhega.
3-4 error classes kaafi hain. Agar caller do errors mein farak nahi karega to unhe alag mat banao.

lessons.name: Debugging — console methods, debugger statement, DevTools profiling
lessons.desc: console.table/warn/error/group for structured logging. debugger statement pauses execution. DevTools Profiler shows CPU usage. Network tab shows requests. Memory tab detects leaks. Source maps help debug minified code.
lessons.q: What console methods do you use for debugging? When would you use console.table vs console.log?
lessons.qsub: How do you use the DevTools profiler to find slow functions? What are source maps and how do they work?
terms: Code mein likha ek shabd jo DevTools khula ho to wahan rok deta hai.
Wo line jahan code ruk jaaye taaki state dekh sako.
Minified code ko wapas asli code se jodne wali file.
lessons.what: console.log se aage bhi bahut kuch hai — aur uska aadha hissa debugging ka waqt aadha kar deta hai.
lessons.why: console.log se kaam chal jaata hai, par usme aap sirf wahi dekh paate ho jo pehle se socha tha. Breakpoint par poori state ek saath dikhti hai — saare variables, poora call stack. Isliye ek breakpoint aksar das console.log se tez hota hai.
where: Source maps ke bina minified stack bekaar hai.
Performance tab se seedha slow function tak.
pros: Breakpoint par poori state dikh jaati hai — log se kahin behtar.
Conditional breakpoints se loop ke ek chakkar par ruk sakte ho.
Logpoints se code badle bina log mil jaata hai.
cons: Async code mein stack toot jaata hai.
Production mein source maps ke bina kuch samajh nahi aata.
Minified third-party code debug karna lagbhag namumkin.
gotchas: console.log(obj) object ka live reference dikhata hai — baad ki value dikh sakti hai. Snapshot ke liye console.log(structuredClone(obj)).
debugger line production mein kabhi mat chhodo — linter rule laga do.
console.log({ user }) likho, console.log(user) nahi — naam bhi dikh jaata hai.

lessons.name: Callbacks & Callback Hell
lessons.desc: Passing a function to be executed after an async operation — leads to nested "pyramid of doom".
lessons.q: What is a callback? What is callback hell and what problems does it cause?
lessons.qsub: How do Promises solve callback hell?
terms: Wo function jo aap kisi aur ko de dete ho — "kaam khatam ho jaaye to ise chala dena".
Callbacks ke andar callbacks — code daayein taraf jhukta chala jaata hai.
lessons.what:
JS ko kuch lamba kaam karna ho (network, file, timer), to wo ruk kar wait nahi karta. Aap use ek function de dete ho: "jab ho jaaye to ise chala dena". Wahi callback hai.

Problem tab aati hai jab ek kaam ke baad doosra, phir teesra — har ek dusre ke andar ghusta jaata hai.
lessons.why: Callback hell sirf dikhne mein bura nahi tha — error handling uska asli dard tha. Har level par alag se error check karna padta tha, aur ek bhool jaao to error chup-chaap gayab. Promises isi dard ke jawab mein aaye.

visual.cap: Callback nesting daayein badhti jaati hai aur har level ka apna error check chahiye. Promise chain neeche seedhi chalti hai, ek hi catch sab sambhal leta hai.

where: addEventListener aaj bhi callback hi leta hai — promises yahan fit nahi hote.
map, filter ko diya function bhi callback hai (par sync).
Node ki purani APIs sab callback-based hain — pehchanna zaroori hai.
pros: Sabse simple idea — koi extra concept nahi.
Events ke liye aaj bhi sabse sahi tarika.
Promise se halka — koi microtask overhead nahi.
cons: Nesting se code daayein jhukta jaata hai.
Error har level par handle karna padta hai.
Callback ko galti se do baar bula dena aasan hai.
gotchas: Node style mein error pehla argument hota hai — (err, data). Bhoolna aam galti hai.
Callback ke andar throw karne se wo bahar ke try/catch mein nahi pakda jaata.
Purani callback API ko promise mein badalne ke liye util.promisify ya khud new Promise wrapper.

lessons.name: Event Loop
lessons.desc: The mechanism that lets JS be non-blocking: picks tasks from the queue when the call stack is empty.
lessons.q: Explain the event loop. What is the difference between the microtask queue and macrotask queue?
lessons.qsub: What is the order of output for: setTimeout, Promise.then, queueMicrotask?
terms: Jo kaam abhi chal raha hai uski dher. Ek waqt mein ek.
VIP line — Promise.then, await ke baad ka code.
lessons.what:
JS ek waqt mein ek hi kaam karta hai. Phir 5 second ka network call page ko jam kyu nahi karta?

Kyunki JS wo kaam khud nahi karta — browser ko de deta hai aur aage badh jaata hai. Jawab aane par wo ek line mein lag jaata hai. Event loop wo chowkidaar hai jo poochta rehta hai: "stack khaali hai? To line se agla utha lo."
lessons.analogy: Doctor (stack) ek waqt mein ek mareez. Blood test lab ko bhej diya, agla mareez dekh liya. Report aane par wo waiting line mein lagti hai. Aur do lines hain — VIP (promises) aur normal (setTimeout).
lessons.why: Iske bina har network call par poora page jam ho jaata. Aur samajhna isliye zaroori hai kyunki interview ke output-order sawaal aur "mera state update turant kyu nahi dikha?" — dono ka jawab yahi hai.

visual.cap: Sabse zaroori niyam: har EK macrotask ke baad POORI microtask line khaali hoti hai — tabhi agla macrotask uthta hai.

lessons.name: Microtasks vs Macrotasks
lessons.desc: Microtasks (Promise callbacks, queueMicrotask) run before the next macrotask (setTimeout, setInterval).
lessons.q: What is the difference between microtasks and macrotasks? Predict the output of a tricky async snippet.
lessons.qsub: Why do microtasks have priority over macrotasks?
terms: Microtasks khatam hi na hon to macrotasks kabhi nahi chalte — page jam.
lessons.what:
Do alag lines hain, aur unka niyam ek line mein: ek macrotask chalao → poori microtask line khaali karo → tab agla macrotask.

Isliye Promise.then hamesha setTimeout(fn, 0) se pehle chalta hai, chahe setTimeout pehle likha ho.
lessons.why: Microtask queue isliye banayi gayi taaki promise ka jawab agle paint se pehle mil jaaye. Warna har .then ek poora frame late hota aur UI phatak-phatak karta.
where: Output-order wale sawaal sidhe isi se aate hain.
DOM update ke turant baad padhne ke liye microtask; agle frame ke liye requestAnimationFrame.
Bada kaam todna ho to setTimeout use karo taaki browser paint kar sake.
pros: Promises ka order hamesha tay aur predictable.
Microtask paint se pehle chalta hai — UI turant sahi dikhta hai.
Ek hi mental model se saara async order samajh aa jaata hai.
cons: Microtask chain page ko bhookha rakh sakti hai (starvation).
Do queues yaad rakhni padti hain.
Node ka model thoda alag hai (process.nextTick, phases).
gotchas: process.nextTick (Node) microtask se bhi pehle chalta hai — alag queue hai.
Bhaari kaam todne ke liye setTimeout (macro) chahiye — microtask se todoge to browser paint hi nahi karega.
Interview mein "microtask kya hai" ka jawab: ek macrotask ke baad poori microtask line khaali hoti hai — bas yahi line kaafi hai.

lessons.name: Promises
lessons.desc: Objects representing eventual completion or failure of an async operation, with then/catch chaining.
lessons.q: Explain how a Promise works internally. What are the three states?
lessons.qsub: Implement Promise.all, Promise.race, Promise.allSettled from scratch.
terms: Ek dabba jo kehta hai "jawab abhi nahi hai, par aayega — ya to value ya error".
Teen haalatein. Ek baar pending se nikal gaya to phir kabhi nahi badalta.
.then() hamesha naya promise deta hai — isliye chain banti hai.
lessons.what:
Promise ek rasid hai. Kaam abhi khatam nahi hua, par aapke paas ek cheez hai jispe aap keh sakte ho "jab ho jaaye to mujhe batana".

Uski teen haalatein hain: pending (chal raha hai), fulfilled (ho gaya, value hai), rejected (fail hua, error hai). Ek baar tay ho gaya to hamesha ke liye tay — dobara nahi badalta.
lessons.analogy: Dhobi ki rasid. Kapde abhi nahi mile, par rasid mil gayi. Kapde aa gaye = fulfilled. Kho gaye = rejected. Aur ek baar decide ho gaya to badal nahi sakta.
lessons.why: Promise ne callback ke do sabse bade dard theek kiye: nesting (chain seedhi neeche chalti hai) aur error handling (ek .catch() poori chain sambhal leta hai).

visual.cap: Ek baar pending se nikla to hamesha ke liye tay. .then chain banati hai, aur koi bhi step fail ho to seedha .catch par kood jaata hai.

Wo promises ke upar ek chhoti chaadar hai — andar yahi chal raha hota hai.
pros: Chain seedhi neeche chalti hai — nesting khatam.
Ek .catch() poori chain ke errors sambhal leta hai.
Combinators (all, race) se parallel kaam aasan.
cons: Ek baar shuru hua to cancel nahi kar sakte (AbortController alag se chahiye).
.then mein return bhoolna chain tod deta hai — chup-chaap.
Nested promises abhi bhi likhe ja sakte hain — promise apne aap flat nahi karta.
gotchas: .then ke andar return lagana zaroori hai — warna agla step undefined paayega.
Promise turant chal padta hai banate hi — .then lagane ka intezaar nahi karta.
.catch lagana bhoole to "unhandled rejection" — aur Node mein wo process crash kar sakta hai.

lessons.name: async / await
lessons.desc: Syntactic sugar over Promises that makes async code look synchronous using generator-like pausing.
lessons.q: How does async/await work under the hood? What does await actually do?
lessons.qsub: What happens if you forget to await a Promise? How do you handle errors with async/await?
terms: Function ko promise lautane wala bana deta hai.
Promise ke jawab ka intezaar — par thread block nahi hota.
lessons.what:
async/await koi nayi cheez nahi hai — wo promises ke upar chhota syntax hai. Andar wahi promises chal rahe hote hain.

await ka matlab hai: "yahan ruk jao, jawab aane par aage badhna". Par wo poore program ko nahi rokta — sirf ye function rukta hai; baaki code chalta rehta hai.
lessons.why: Promise chain padhne mein achhi thi, par loops aur if-else uske andar ajeeb ho jaate the. await se async code bilkul normal sync code jaisa dikhne lagta hai — try/catch bhi wapas kaam karne lagta hai.
where: Har data fetching aaj isi tarah likhi jaati hai.
Jab agla step pichhle ke jawab par depend kare.
pros: Async code sync jaisa padhne layak ho jaata hai.
try/catch, loops, if-else — sab normal chalte hain.
Debugger step-through theek se kaam karta hai.
cons: Ek ke baad ek await likhne se code bekaar mein slow ho jaata hai.
Har async function promise lautata hai — bhoolne par [object Promise] print hota hai.
Top-level await sirf ES modules mein chalta hai.
gotchas: Sabse badi galti: aisi cheezon ko ek-ek karke await karna jo saath chal sakti thin. Promise.all use karo.
forEach ke andar await kaam nahi karta — for...of use karo.
async function ko await ke bina bulaya aur wo fail ho gaya, to "unhandled rejection" milega.

lessons.name: Promise Combinators
lessons.desc: Promise.all, .race, .allSettled, .any — each handles multiple concurrent promises differently.
lessons.q: When would you use Promise.all vs Promise.allSettled vs Promise.race vs Promise.any?
lessons.qsub: What happens to Promise.all if one promise rejects?
terms: Sab safal hon tabhi safal. Ek bhi fail → poora fail.
Sabka intezaar karo, chahe fail hon — sabka result do.
Jo pehle khatam ho (safal ya fail), wahi jawab.
Jo pehle SAFAL ho. Sab fail hon tabhi fail.
lessons.what: Chaar tareeke hain kai promises ko ek saath sambhalne ke. Farak sirf ek baat mein hai: kab khatam maana jaaye, aur fail hone par kya karein.
lessons.why: Ek-ek karke await likhne se kaam bekaar mein slow ho jaata hai — teen API call jo saath chal sakti thin, wo 3 guna time lengi. Combinators isi ka ilaaj hain. Aur allSettled ek aur dard theek karta hai: ek widget fail ho to poora page nahi girna chahiye.

race se network call par time limit.
any se kai mirrors mein jo pehle chale.
pros: Parallel kaam se bahut time bachta hai.
allSettled se ek fail poora page nahi girata.
race se timeout bina extra library ke.
cons: all mein ek fail hone par baaki ke safal results bhi gayab ho jaate hain.
race haare hue promises ko cancel nahi karta — wo chalte rehte hain.
any purane browsers mein nahi hai.
gotchas: Promise.all promises banate hi chal padte hain — array banate waqt hi sab shuru ho jaate hain.
UI ke liye aksar allSettled sahi hota hai, all nahi — ek widget fail ho to poora page nahi girna chahiye.
race ke baad haara hua request abhi bhi chal raha hai — sach mein rokne ke liye AbortController chahiye.

lessons.name: Async Error Handling — unhandled rejections, .catch(), global handlers
lessons.desc: Unhandled promise rejections crash Node.js (>=15). Always .catch() or use try/await. window.onunhandledrejection catches browser unhandled rejections. process.on("unhandledRejection") for Node. Error boundaries catch React render errors.
lessons.q: What happens when a Promise rejects without a .catch()? How do you handle async errors globally?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between an unhandled rejection and an uncaught exception? How does React Error Boundary handle async errors?
terms: Aisa rejected promise jispe koi .catch nahi laga.
Aakhri jaal — jo error kahin nahi pakda gaya, wo yahan aata hai.
lessons.what:
Async errors sync errors se alag behave karte hain, aur yahi sabse zyada bugs banata hai.

Do niyam: (1) callback ke andar ka throw bahar ke try/catch mein nahi aata. (2) Promise par .catch na ho to error chup-chaap gayab (aur Node mein process crash).
lessons.why: Sync error crash kar deta hai — dikh jaata hai. Async error chup-chaap gayab ho jaata hai. Yahi wajah hai ki production mein sabse zyada chhupe hue bugs async errors hote hain, aur isliye har promise par await ya .catch ka niyam banana padta hai.
where: await ho ya .catch — dono mein se ek zaroori.
Analytics jaisi calls par bhi .catch lagao.
Global handlers se wo errors milte hain jo aap miss kar gaye.
pros: async/await se normal try/catch wapas kaam karta hai.
Global handlers aakhri safety net dete hain.
allSettled se ek fail poora page nahi girata.
cons: Floating promise ka error chup-chaap gayab hota hai.
Async stack traces chhote aur kam kaam ke hote hain.
forEach + async ka trap bahut aam hai.
gotchas: Har promise par await ya .catch — dono mein se ek zaroori hai. Warna error gayab.
forEach(async ...) kabhi mat likho — for...of ya Promise.all.
Node 15+ mein unhandled rejection process crash kar deti hai — production mein handler zaroori.

lessons.name: Garbage Collection
lessons.desc: Automatic memory management using mark-and-sweep: objects with no reachable references are freed.
lessons.q: How does JavaScript garbage collection work? What can cause memory leaks?
lessons.qsub: Explain 3 common memory leak patterns in JS applications.
terms: JS ka khud purani memory free karna.
Wo object jis tak root (global, stack) se koi raasta bacha ho.
GC ka tarika: root se chal kar sab reachable ko mark karo, baaki saaf kar do.
lessons.what:
JS mein memory aap free nahi karte — engine karta hai. Uska niyam ek hi hai: jo object ab reachable nahi hai, wo saaf ho jaayega.

Reachable matlab: global, current stack, ya kisi reachable object se uska koi raasta bacha ho.
lessons.analogy: Ghar mein saaman: jo cheez kisi ne pakdi hui hai wo rakhi rehti hai. Jise koi nahi pakde hue, wo kabaad mein chali jaati hai. Baat "purana hai kya" ki nahi hai — "koi pakde hue hai kya" ki hai.
lessons.why: Isliye memory leak ka matlab "purana object" nahi hota — matlab hota hai "koi abhi bhi use pakde hue hai jabki zarurat nahi". Aur ye pakad aksar closures, listeners aur global arrays mein chhupi hoti hai.

Bina limit ka cache hamesha ek leak hai.
pros: Memory khud manage nahi karni padti.
Circular references modern GC ke liye problem nahi.
Zyadatar app-level code mein GC ke baare mein sochna hi nahi padta.
cons: GC kab chalega ye aap tay nahi kar sakte.
GC pause animation mein hichki de sakta hai.
Leak dhundhna mushkil — koi error nahi milti, bas memory badhti hai.
gotchas: Circular reference JS mein leak nahi hai — mark-and-sweep root se dekhta hai. Ye purana IE-era mith hai.
Closure poore scope ko pakad sakta hai, sirf use ki gayi variable ko nahi — bade objects par dhyaan do.
WeakMap/WeakSet ki key ko GC saaf kar sakta hai — cache ke liye best.

lessons.name: WeakMap / WeakSet / WeakRef
lessons.desc: WeakMap keys must be objects and are weakly held (GC can collect them). WeakSet holds objects weakly. Use WeakMap for private data, caching, and metadata without preventing garbage collection.
lessons.q: What is a WeakMap? How does it differ from Map in terms of garbage collection?
lessons.qsub: How would you use WeakMap to implement a private class field? What are the limitations of WeakMap?
terms: Keys ko pakadta nahi — GC unhe saaf kar sakta hai.
Aisa collection jo memory leak nahi banata.
lessons.what:
Normal Map apni keys ko pakad kar rakhta hai. To agar key ek DOM node hai aur wo page se hat jaaye, wo phir bhi memory mein rahegi — kyunki Map use pakde hue hai.

WeakMap pakadta nahi. Object kahin aur se reachable na ho to wo aur uski entry dono saaf.
lessons.why: Isliye jab key ka jeevan aapke control mein na ho (DOM nodes, user objects, third-party objects), WeakMap hi sahi choice hai — cleanup ka code likhna hi nahi padta.
where: Node ke saath data jodna bina leak ke.
Memoize jahan key ek object ho.
User ke objects par apna data, bina unhe zinda rakhe.
pros: Leak apne aap ruk jaata hai — cleanup code nahi likhna.
DOM/object metadata ke liye sabse safe.
Third-party objects ke saath bhi safe.
cons: Iterate nahi kar sakte, size nahi.
Keys sirf objects.
Debug karna mushkil — content dekhne ka tarika hi nahi.
gotchas: Keys sirf objects — string/number daalne par TypeError.
Iterate na kar paana jaan-boojh kar hai — warna GC ka behaviour observable ho jaata.
Chunav ka niyam: key ka jeevan aapke control mein hai? Haan → Map. Nahi → WeakMap.

lessons.name: Memory Leaks
lessons.desc: When objects remain in memory unintentionally — detached DOM nodes, forgotten timers, global variables.
lessons.q: What are the most common memory leak patterns? How do you detect and fix them?
lessons.qsub: How would you debug a memory leak in a production React app?
terms: Aisi memory jo ab zarurat nahi, par kuch use pakde hue hai isliye free nahi hoti.
Wo DOM node jo page se hat gaya par JS abhi bhi use pakde hue hai.
lessons.what:
Leak ka matlab "memory bhar gayi" nahi hai — matlab hai kisi ne kuch pakad rakha hai jiski zarurat khatam ho chuki hai.

JS mein iske chaar hi bade karan hain, aur chaaron pehchanne layak hain.
lessons.why: SPA mein ye sabse bada issue hai. Page reload nahi hota, isliye har screen change par thoda-thoda leak jamta rehta hai — aur ghante bhar baad app slow ho jaata hai ya crash.
where: Route change par cleanup na karna — sabse aam wajah.
Dashboard jo ghanton khula rehta hai — wahan chhota leak bhi bada ban jaata hai.
pros: Chaar hi patterns hain — pehchanne ke baad rokna aasan.
DevTools se saaf dikh jaate hain (heap snapshot compare).
WeakMap/AbortController se kai apne aap theek ho jaate hain.
cons: Koi error nahi milti — chup-chaap app slow hota hai.
Dhoondhne mein waqt lagta hai.
Third-party library ke leak par aapka control nahi hota.
gotchas: Anonymous function se listener lagaya to use remove nahi kar sakte — reference rakho.
AbortController ek signal se saare listeners ek saath hata deta hai — sabse saaf tarika.
DevTools mein "Detached HTMLDivElement" dikhna seedha leak ka nishaan hai.

lessons.name: Lazy Evaluation
lessons.desc: Deferring computation until the value is actually needed — generators, Proxy, and on-demand patterns.
lessons.q: What is lazy evaluation? How can generators enable lazy sequences in JS?
lessons.qsub: How does React lazy() use this concept?
terms: Kaam tabhi karo jab jawab sach mein chahiye.
Sab kuch pehle hi kar dalo — chahe zarurat pade ya na pade.
&& / || ka jawab pata chalte hi ruk jaana.
lessons.what:
Lazy ka matlab: calculate mat karo jab tak koi maange nahi.

JS mein ye kai jagah pehle se hai — &&/|| ka short-circuit, generators, aur dynamic import().
lessons.why: Bade apps mein zyadatar code user kabhi use hi nahi karta. Sab kuch pehle load karoge to page khulne mein hi der lagegi. Lazy soch kehti hai: jo abhi chahiye wahi lao, baaki jab maange tab. Yahi wajah hai ki modern apps chhote bundles mein split hote hain.
where: Dynamic import() — bundle chhota rehta hai, page tez khulta hai.
loading="lazy" — screen par aane par hi load.
Virtualization — sirf dikhne wale rows render karo.
pros: Bekaar ka kaam bilkul hota hi nahi.
Initial load bahut tez ho jaata hai.
Infinite sequences mumkin ho jaate hain.
cons: Kaam baad mein hota hai — us waqt user ko delay dikhta hai.
Debug karna mushkil — "ye kab chala?"
Zyada lazy karne se code samajhna mushkil ho jaata hai.
gotchas: a || b() mein b() chalta hi nahi agar a truthy ho — side effect wahan mat rakho.
Lazy karne ke liye function pass karo, value nahi — value pass karte hi wo calculate ho jaati hai.
import() promise deta hai — await ya .then chahiye.

lessons.name: Debounce & Throttle
lessons.desc: Debounce delays execution until activity stops; throttle limits execution to at most once per interval.
lessons.q: What is the difference between debounce and throttle? Implement both from scratch.
lessons.qsub: When would you use debounce on a search input vs throttle on a scroll handler?
terms: Shaant hone ka intezaar — user ruk jaaye tab chalao.
Ek time mein ek baar — bhale user kitna bhi kare.
lessons.what:
Dono taaki bar-bar chalne wala kaam kam ho — par soch ulti hai:

Debounce: "jab tak event aate rahenge, main rukа rahunga. Ruk jaaye to chalunga."
Throttle: "main har X ms mein ek baar zaroor chalunga, chahe event kitne bhi aayein."
lessons.why: Bina inke, search box mein har keystroke par API call jaayegi aur scroll par har frame calculation chalegi — dono se app slow aur server par bekaar load. Ye do chhote functions us poore dard ka ilaaj hain, aur dono closure par khade hain (timer kahan rakha hai — wahi closure mein).
