where: Debounce — har keystroke par API call nahi karni.
Throttle — har frame par calculate nahi karna.
Throttle — button dabane par ek hi request jaaye.
pros: API calls aur re-renders bahut kam ho jaate hain.
Dono ~10 line mein khud likhe ja sakte hain (interview mein poocha jaata hai).
Closure ka sabse saaf real-world use.
cons: Debounce mein user ko delay dikhta hai.
Galat wala chun liya to behaviour ulta lagta hai.
React mein har render par naya debounce ban jaata hai — useMemo/useRef chahiye.
gotchas: Chunav ka niyam: aakhri value chahiye → debounce. Beech ke updates bhi chahiye → throttle.
React mein debounce ko useMemo ke bina banaya to har render par naya banega aur kaam nahi karega.
Component hatte waqt clearTimeout karna zaroori hai — warna hate hue component par setState.

lessons.name: Web Workers
lessons.desc: Run JS on a background thread separate from the main thread to avoid blocking the UI.
lessons.q: What are Web Workers? What are their limitations? How do they communicate with the main thread?
lessons.qsub: What is a SharedArrayBuffer and why is it useful with Workers?
terms: Ek alag thread jahan JS chalta hai — main thread ko block kiye bina.
Worker aur main thread ke beech baat karne ka tarika.
Message bhejte waqt data ki copy banti hai — reference nahi jaata.
lessons.what:
JS main thread par ek waqt mein ek kaam. Bhaari calculation poora UI jam kar deti hai.

Worker ek alag thread deta hai. Wahan calculation chalti rahegi aur UI chalta rahega. Baat postMessage se hoti hai.
lessons.why: Ye ek hi cheez hai jo sach mein main thread ko free karti hai. setTimeout se kaam todna madad karta hai par kaam abhi bhi main thread par hi hai. Worker use bilkul hata deta hai.
where: Image processing, bada JSON parse, encryption.
Ek khaas worker jo network requests beech mein pakadta hai (alag topic).
pros: UI bilkul jam nahi hota — asli parallelism.
Multi-core CPU ka faayda milta hai.
Crash ho jaaye to main page safe rehta hai.
cons: DOM nahi milta — sirf calculation kar sakte ho.
Message bhejne mein data ki copy banti hai — bade data par mehnga.
Alag file chahiye, aur setup ka thoda jhanjhat.
gotchas: Worker ko DOM nahi milta — window, document kuch nahi. Sirf calculation.
Data copy hota hai, share nahi — bade array ke liye Transferable use karo.
Worker ko terminate() karna zaroori hai, warna wo chalta rehta hai.

lessons.name: ES Modules vs CommonJS
lessons.desc: ESM uses import/export (static, tree-shakable); CJS uses require() (dynamic, synchronous).
lessons.q: What is the difference between ES Modules and CommonJS? Why does it matter for bundlers?
lessons.qsub: What is tree-shaking and how do ES Modules enable it?
terms: Bundler ka unused code hata dena — sirf ESM mein mumkin.
lessons.what:
Do system hain code ko files mein baantne ke. Sabse bada farak: ESM chalne se pehle padha jaata hai (static), CommonJS chalte waqt (dynamic).

Isi ek farak se sab kuch nikalta hai — tree shaking, top-level await, aur circular imports ka behaviour.
lessons.why: ESM static hai, isliye bundler chalne se pehle dekh sakta hai ki kaunsa code use hi nahi ho raha — aur use hata deta hai (tree shaking). CommonJS mein require kahin bhi, kisi bhi condition mein ho sakta hai, isliye ye pakka pata hi nahi chalta.
where: ESM hi standard hai — Vite, Rollup, browsers sab.
pros: Tree shaking se bundle bahut chhota.
Static analysis — editor autocomplete aur errors behtar.
Top-level await aur dynamic import.
cons: Purani Node libraries CommonJS mein hain — mixing dard deta hai.
ESM mein file extension (.js) likhna zaroori hai.
__dirname ESM mein nahi milta.
gotchas: ESM mein import hoist hote hain — file mein kahin bhi likho, chalte sabse pehle hain.
ESM live binding deta hai (value badle to dikhega), CommonJS copy deta hai.
ESM hamesha strict mode mein chalta hai, chahe likha ho ya nahi.

lessons.name: Singleton Pattern
lessons.desc: Ensures only one instance of an object exists — commonly used for config stores or DB connections.
lessons.q: Implement the Singleton pattern in JavaScript. What are its downsides?
lessons.qsub: How does ES Modules naturally solve the singleton problem?
terms: Aisa pattern jisme poore app mein us cheez ka ek hi instance ho.
Aisi cheez jo poore app mein ek ho aur kahin se bhi chhui ja sake.
lessons.what:
"Is cheez ka poore app mein ek hi hona chahiye" — jaise ek database connection, ek config, ek logger.

JS mein iska sabse saaf tarika alag hai: module khud singleton hai. Module ek hi baar chalta hai aur uska export cache ho jaata hai — to bas ek object export kar do.
lessons.why:
Par imaandari se: Singleton asal mein global variable hai, class ke mukhaute mein. Uske teen nuksaan hain — test mein ek test ki state agle mein reh jaati hai, nirbharta code mein dikhti nahi, aur badalna mushkil ho jaata hai.

Aksar behtar hai: ek instance banao aur use pass kar do (dependency injection).
where: App settings — module export sabse saaf.
Ek hi logger poore app mein.
Redux store, query client — ek hi instance.
pros: JS mein module hone ki wajah se lagbhag muft milta hai.
Bhaari resource (connection pool) ek hi baar banta hai.
Kahin se bhi access — shuru mein suvidha lagti hai.
cons: Global state — test order matter karne lagta hai.
Nirbharta chhup jaati hai — code padh kar pata nahi chalta.
Concrete class se bandh jaate ho, interface se nahi.
gotchas: JS mein module hi singleton hai — getInstance() likhne ki zarurat hi nahi. Interview mein ye bata dena achha signal hai.
Singleton test ko flaky banata hai — state reset karne ka tarika rakho.
"Thread safety" ka sawaal JS mein lagta hi nahi — wo single-threaded hai.

lessons.name: Factory Pattern
lessons.desc: A function or class that creates and returns objects without the caller knowing the exact type.
lessons.q: What is the factory pattern? How does it differ from using the new keyword directly?
lessons.qsub: When would you choose a factory function over a class?
terms: Ek function jo object banata hai — caller ko "kaunsa" ka faisla nahi karna padta.
JS mein class ke bina object banane ka aam tarika.
lessons.what:
Object banane ka faisla ek jagah rakho. Caller bas kehta hai "mujhe ye chahiye" — kaunsi class banegi, ye factory tay karti hai.

JS mein iska ek aur roop hai: factory function — new ke bina object banana, closure ke saath private data.
lessons.why: Bahar se aaya data (form, JSON, API) ko objects mein badalne ke liye kahin na kahin if-else lagana hi padta hai. Factory wo if-else ek jagah rakh deti hai — poore codebase mein bikhrne ki jagah.
where: JSON ko domain objects mein badalna.
Factory function + closure — class ka aasan alternative.
pros: Banane ka faisla ek jagah — badalna aasan.
Factory function mein this ka jhanjhat hi nahi.
Registry se naya type jodna ek line ka kaam.
cons: Har object apni methods ki copy rakhta hai (prototype share nahi hota) — hazaron objects par memory.
Ek aur layer — chhoti cheezon ke liye zarurat nahi.
instanceof kaam nahi karta factory function ke saath.
gotchas: Factory function mein har object ko methods ki apni copy milti hai — bade paimane par class/prototype behtar hai.
Factory ka switch theek hai — wahi ek jagah hai jahan wo hona chahiye. Use har jagah copy mat karo.
Interview mein "factory function vs constructor" poocha jaaye to: closure privacy vs prototype memory — ye trade-off batao.

lessons.name: Observer / PubSub Pattern
lessons.desc: Objects subscribe to events; publisher notifies all subscribers — decouples sender from receivers.
lessons.q: Implement a simple EventEmitter (on, emit, off) from scratch.
lessons.qsub: How does Node.js EventEmitter compare to the browser EventTarget API?
terms: Kuch hua to jinhe matlab hai unhe khabar mil jaaye.
Wo cheez jispe kuch hota hai.
lessons.what:
Ek cheez badle to jinhe matlab hai unhe khud-ba-khud pata chal jaaye — aur badalne wale ko ye jaanne ki zarurat na ho ki kaun sun raha hai.

Aap ye pehle se use karte ho: addEventListener bilkul yahi hai.
lessons.why: Isse bhejne wala aur sunne wala alag ho jaate hain. Naye listeners jodne par purana code ek line nahi badalta — yahi iska poora faayda hai.
where: Redux, Zustand — sab subscribe/notify par khade hain.
Do door ke components ke beech baat, bina props drilling.
pros: Bhejne wale ko sunne walon ka pata nahi — poora decoupling.
Naye listeners = zero change purane code mein.
Ek event, kai reactions.
cons: Flow follow karna mushkil — "ye kahan se trigger hua?"
Unsubscribe bhoolna seedha memory leak.
Zyada event bus se code ka control flow bikhar jaata hai.
gotchas: Har listener ko try/catch mein lapetо — warna ek buggy listener baaki sabko rok dega.
on() se hamesha unsubscribe function wapas do — cleanup aasan ho jaata hai.
Global event bus ka zyada use debugging ko narak bana deta hai — pehle props/context sochо.

lessons.name: DOM Manipulation & Reflow
lessons.desc: Changing the DOM triggers layout recalculation (reflow) and repainting — expensive in bulk.
lessons.q: What is the difference between repaint and reflow? How do you batch DOM changes to minimise cost?
lessons.qsub: What is DocumentFragment and why is it useful?
terms: Browser dobara naapta hai ki kya kahan hai — mehnga.
Sirf rang/dikhawat badalna — reflow se sasta.
Baar-baar likhna-padhna, jisse har baar reflow force hota hai.
lessons.what:
DOM badalna JS ka sabse mehnga kaam hai. Har badlav browser ko dobara layout naapne (reflow) ya paint karne par majboor kar sakta hai.

Sabse bada bug: layout thrashing — loop mein likho, phir padho, phir likho. Har padhne par browser ko turant reflow karna padta hai.
lessons.why: Browser badlav ko batch karta hai — sab jama karke ek baar mein karta hai. Par jaise hi aap offsetHeight jaisa kuch padhte ho, use majboori mein abhi calculate karna padta hai. Loop mein ye 1000 reflow ban jaata hai.

Position padhna throttle karo, warna har frame reflow.

transform se animation GPU par chali jaati hai.

Har browser thoda alag optimize karta hai.
Zyada optimize karne se code padhna mushkil.

Loop mein appendChild ki jagah DocumentFragment use karo.
innerHTML += poora subtree dobara banata hai — kabhi loop mein mat likho.

lessons.name: Event Delegation
lessons.desc: Attaching a single listener to a parent instead of many children — exploits event bubbling.
lessons.q: What is event delegation? Why is it a performance pattern? When does it fail?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between event.target and event.currentTarget?
terms: Event child se shuru hokar upar parents tak jaata hai.
Har child par listener lagane ki jagah ek parent par lagana.
Wo element jispe asal mein click hua.
lessons.what:
1000 rows hain aur har row par delete button. 1000 listeners lagaoge?

Nahi — ek listener parent par lagao. Event bubble hokar wahan aayega, aur e.target se pata chal jaayega ki kis par click hua.
lessons.why: Do bade faayde: memory (1000 ki jagah 1 listener) aur naye elements apne aap kaam karte hain — kyunki listener parent par hai, naye child ko alag se listener lagane ki zarurat hi nahi.

Naye elements bina extra kaam ke chalte hain.
Cleanup aasan — ek hi listener hataana hai.

focus/blur bubble nahi karte — ye kaam nahi karega.

lessons.name: fetch / XMLHttpRequest
lessons.desc: Fetch is a modern Promise-based HTTP API; XHR is the older callback/event approach.
lessons.q: How does fetch work? What does it return? How is it different from axios?
lessons.qsub: What are the limitations of fetch that axios solves (e.g., request cancellation, interceptors)?
terms: Promise-based network API — aaj ka standard.
Chal rahi request ko cancel karne ka tarika.
lessons.what:
fetch promise deta hai aur padhne mein saaf hai. Par uski ek cheez sabko chaunkati hai:

fetch 404 ya 500 par reject nahi hota. Wo sirf network fail (internet gaya) par reject hota hai. Status khud check karna padta hai.
lessons.why: Ye jaan-boojh kar hai — "response mil gaya" aur "response achha tha" do alag baatein hain. Par isi wajah se sabse aam bug aata hai: log .catch laga kar samajh lete hain ki errors handle ho gaye.
where: fetch aaj default hai — XHR sirf purane code mein.
Search-as-you-type mein purani request abort karna.
XHR abhi bhi zaroori hai — fetch mein upload progress nahi milta.
pros: Promise-based — async/await ke saath saaf.
AbortController se cancel aur timeout.
Streaming responses support karta hai.
cons: HTTP error par reject nahi hota — har jagah res.ok check karna padta hai.
Upload progress nahi milta (XHR mein milta hai).
Cookies default mein cross-origin nahi jaati — credentials set karna padta hai.
gotchas: fetch 404/500 par reject nahi hota — if (!res.ok) throw likhna zaroori hai.
Response body ek hi baar padh sakte ho — dobara chahiye to res.clone().
Har API call ke liye ek chhota wrapper likh lo — res.ok check bhoolna band ho jaayega.

lessons.name: Browser Storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies)
lessons.desc: Four client-side storage mechanisms with different persistence, capacity, and security characteristics.
lessons.q: Compare localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, and IndexedDB. When do you use each?
lessons.qsub: What are the security considerations around storing tokens in localStorage vs httpOnly cookies?
terms: ~5MB, hamesha ke liye rehta hai, sync (blocking).
Wahi, par tab band hote hi mit jaata hai.
~4KB, har request ke saath server ko jaata hai.
lessons.what: Chaar jagah hain browser mein data rakhne ki. Chunav teen sawaal se hota hai: kitna bada, kab tak rahe, aur server ko chahiye ya nahi.
lessons.why: Galat jagah chunne ka nuksaan asli hai. Auth token localStorage mein rakha to XSS use padh sakta hai. Bada data localStorage mein rakha to sync hone ki wajah se UI freeze hoga. Aur bada data cookie mein rakha to har request bhaari ho jaayegi. Isliye chunav soch kar karna padta hai.

IndexedDB mein GBs data aur objects seedha rakh sakte ho.

cons: localStorage synchronous hai — bada data likhna main thread block karta hai.
Sirf string — har baar JSON convert karna padta hai.
Cookie har request mein jaati hai — bada karoge to har request bhaari.

localStorage private/incognito mode mein throw kar sakta hai — hamesha try/catch.
localStorage sync hai — 5MB likhoge to UI freeze hoga. Bade data ke liye IndexedDB.

lessons.name: Service Workers & Cache API
lessons.desc: Background scripts that intercept network requests — enable offline-first PWAs and cache strategies.
lessons.q: What is a Service Worker? What is its lifecycle? How does it enable offline support?
lessons.qsub: What caching strategies can you implement with a Service Worker?
terms: Ek script jo aapke page aur network ke beech baithti hai.
Requests aur responses store karne ki jagah.
Pehle cache se do, background mein update karo.
lessons.what:
Service worker ek proxy hai jo browser mein chalta hai. Har network request usse hokar jaati hai — aur aap tay kar sakte ho ki cache se dena hai ya network se.

Isi se PWA offline chalte hain.
lessons.why: Bina iske, internet jaate hi app dead. Service worker se aap pehle cache se dikha sakte ho aur background mein taaza data la sakte ho — app turant khulta hai aur offline bhi chalta hai.
where: Assets cache se — repeat visit turant.
pros: App offline bhi chalta hai.
Repeat visits bahut tez.
Background sync aur push notifications.
cons: Debug karna mushkil — purana SW zid se chipka rehta hai.
Sirf HTTPS par chalta hai (localhost chhod kar).
Galat cache strategy se users ko purani app phasti hai.
gotchas: Naya SW purane ke khatam hone ka intezaar karta hai — skipWaiting() aur cache version dono zaroori.
Cache version badalna bhoole to user ko hamesha purani app milegi — ye production ka classic bug hai.
Development mein DevTools → Application → "Update on reload" on rakho.

lessons.name: Regular Expressions — patterns, groups, lookaheads, common pitfalls
lessons.desc: RegExp for pattern matching. Named groups (?<name>), lookaheads (?=...), lookbehinds (?<=...). Common pitfalls: catastrophic backtracking, greedy vs lazy, escaping. Use /u flag for Unicode.
lessons.q: What is the difference between greedy and lazy quantifiers? Give examples.
lessons.qsub: How do you prevent catastrophic backtracking in regex? What is a named capture group?
terms: Text mein pattern dhundhne ka chhota language.
( ) se pakda hua hissa jo alag se nikala ja sake.
(?=...) — "iske aage ye hona chahiye", par match mein shaamil nahi.
lessons.what:
Regex ek chhoti language hai text ke pattern ke liye. Basics 20 minute mein aa jaate hain; baaki reference dekh kar kaam chal jaata hai.

Jo cheezein roz kaam aati hain wo gine-chune hain — neeche wahi hain.
lessons.why: Kuch kaam regex ke bina 20 line lete hain aur regex ke saath ek line. Validation, log parsing, text cleanup — ye teen jagah wo roz kaam aata hai. Par uski keemat bhi hai: likhna aasan, padhna mushkil — isliye complex regex par comment likhna zaroori hai.
where: Log lines, URLs se hisse nikalna.
pros: Ek line mein wo kaam jo 20 line ka hota.
Har language mein lagbhag same — ek baar seekho.
Named groups se padhne layak ho jaata hai.
cons: Likhna aasan, padhna mushkil — 6 mahine baad khud ka regex samajh nahi aata.
Galat regex se catastrophic backtracking (page hang) ho sakta hai.
Email/HTML jaisi cheezein regex se theek se parse hoti hi nahi.
gotchas: .+ greedy hai — jitna kha sakta hai kha jaata hai. Lazy ke liye .+?.
g flag wala regex lastIndex yaad rakhta hai — test() baar-baar bulane par alag jawab deta hai.
HTML regex se parse mat karo — DOMParser use karo. Email ke liye bhi simple check + server verification behtar.

lessons.name: Date/Time — Date, Intl.DateTimeFormat, Temporal API, timezone handling
lessons.desc: Date is notoriously difficult (mutable, poor API). Intl.DateTimeFormat for locale-aware formatting. Temporal API (Stage 3) replaces Date with immutable, timezone-aware types. moment.js/date-fns/luxon are popular alternatives.
lessons.q: What are the problems with JavaScript's Date object? How does the Temporal API improve on it?
lessons.qsub: How do you handle timezone conversions in JavaScript? What is the difference between toISOString and toLocaleString?
terms: JS ka purana date object — bahut sare gotchas ke saath.
Locale ke hisaab se format karne ka built-in tarika.
Naya API jo Date ki saari problems theek karta hai.
lessons.what:
Date JavaScript ka sabse kharab design mana jaata hai — month 0 se shuru, mutable, aur timezone ka behaviour ajeeb.

Aaj ka tarika: formatting ke liye Intl, calculation ke liye library (date-fns/Day.js), aur aage Temporal.
lessons.why: Date JavaScript ka sabse kharab design mana jaata hai — aur uske bugs chup-chaap aate hain (date ek din peeche dikhna, month galat hona). Isliye aaj ka tarika hai: display ke liye Intl, calculation ke liye library, aur server par hamesha ISO string.
where: Intl.DateTimeFormat — locale ke hisaab se, muft mein.
date-fns ya Day.js — Date se seedha mat ladо.
pros: Intl built-in hai aur har locale/timezone sambhalta hai.
ISO string se timezone ka jhagda khatam.
Temporal aane par ye sab bahut saaf ho jaayega.
cons: Month 0-indexed — anginat bugs ki jad.
Date mutable hai — galti se original badal jaata hai.
Timezone handling ke liye library lagbhag zaroori.
gotchas: Month 0 se shuru hota hai par date 1 se. Ye JS ka sabse aam date bug hai.
new Date("2026-08-21") UTC maana jaata hai, "2026-08-21T00:00" local — isse date ek din shift ho jaati hai.
Date mutable hai — setDate original ko badal deta hai. Pehle new Date(d) se copy banao.
